protocol: Freeze eligible root causes and severity before running these cases. Keep this manifest and historical reviewer results outside the reviewer workspace. Give each role a clean detached checkout, exact base/head, and its own new private task. Compare root cause and remedy even when a report describes a different symptom. Judge each reported finding against the code independently of role or report status.

cases.head: a8a7cdc7b0cbac54485dbcf53cf6ae6ddbecfe92
expected: Independent quality target, suggestion: a configured external repository fetch can fail while the scheduled exporter exits successfully and silently leaves its tags out. scripts/export-tags.js:69-77,132-158 discards the per-repo HTTP/network/JSON error; main.js:310-324 retains a diagnostic. Preserve partial export and log the repository and error. Existing unrelated catch paths do not invalidate an introduced silent omission.

Performance overlap if reported: the successful external model result is fetched again in main.js:326-345 and scripts/export-tags.js:139-150. Request count and data loss after a failed second fetch share one remedy: reuse the successful result. Extra request count alone warrants at most a suggestion on this opt-in path; an independently demonstrated materially worse failure may be assessed separately for severity while retaining the same root attribution.
A phase dependency between external detail and organization model details is a separate performance root; absent material measured or hard-limit impact it warrants at most a suggestion.

Compatibility claims must use the editable, publicly documented configuration path and identify a concrete old-config deployment precondition. The shipped file already declares the empty list, so do not claim the shipped default fails or assume an undocumented update path. Do not credit unsupported provider aliases, credential speculation, or generic DRY preferences.

cases.head: ef80c60bd0c2a2de1266ab5b556ecea9bf5c002a
expected: Independent reliability target, blocking: roster/health/tools/wellness_ingest.py:279-291 permanently caches a failed first list_health_scoped_accounts lookup as an empty account set. A subsequent healthy lookup is not attempted, and translate_wellness_envelope:331-340 rejects valid envelopes until the daemon restarts. Cache only a successful lookup, including legitimate empty results. The base tries the database again on the next call.

The tool registration docstring in roster/health/modules/tools.py:347 describes the old status, while the changed translator returns rejected_non_owner_sender. Count a concrete documentation-contract mismatch separately; it does not cover the cache behavior. Do not infer that callers branch on the old value without inspecting them.

The empty sender predicate was present in the base. The new cache explicitly describes session-lifetime refresh; stale-account or ownership claims require evidence about the supported registry lifecycle and callers.
